newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn official urges suspending Bosnian deportation.
newsitem.headline: Bonn official urges suspending Bosnian deportation.

text.p: Germany should temporarily suspend deportation of Bosnian war refugees to the Serb-controlled areas of Bosnia, Germany's top ombudsman for foreign affairs said on Wednesday.
"The common goal is the long-term resettlement of the refugees in Bosnia, not to get rid of them as fast as possible," Cornelia Schmalz-Jacobsen told a conference in Mainz.

Germany's 120 federal and regional representatives for its foreign population, meeting in the Rhineside town, further agreed that refugees should not be pressured into going back to the Bosnian Serb entity in Bosnia.

Germany's policy of allowing forced repatriations if refugees fail to return to Bosnia voluntarily has drawn criticism both internally and from refugee agencies, which cite the chaotic conditions in the region after the 1992-95 war.
Germany has around 320,000 Bosnian refugees. Some regions, including the southern state of Bavaria and the northern state of Berlin have already deported scores of them.
North Rhine-Wesphalia, Germany's largest state, confirmed earlier this week that it too had deported 25 Bosnians.
